item.title: Calabi-Yau at 50: mathematical discovery in the age of AI
item.description: Using the golden jubilee of Yau's proof of the Calabi conjecture as a spring-board, we discuss how the dataset of Calabi-Yau manifolds brought together mathematicians and physicists since the 1980s, and then further brought in the world of machine-learning and AI since 2017. We give a historical account on the growth of the field of ``AI-assisted mathematics'' in the last decade, and comment on what culminated in 2026 as perhaps the most dramatic year in the history of mathematics since Euclid. — Yang-Hui He — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Genus one mirror symmetry and surfaces with trivial first Chern class
item.description: The main goal of this paper is to study the extension of genus-one BCOV type mirror symmetry for smooth projective varieties with vanishing $c_1(X)$. We show that the naive generalization of the expectation that one can encode genus one Gromov-Witten invariants in the BCOV invariant of the mirror family cannot hold in this setup. We show this by completing the study of these invariants for surfaces. Progress had been made recently by Oberdieck's proof of the Klemm-Mari\~no conjecture for Enriques surfaces, which can be combined with computations of equivariant analytic torsion by Yoshikawa. We also perform the analogous study for bielliptic surfaces. Both of these cases present a sign… — Gabriel Ab\'anades-Joglar, Dennis Eriksson — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Teichm\"uller spaces with conical singularities and Virasoro coadjoint orbits
item.description: We study Teichm\"uller spaces of hyperbolic \(0\)-metrics on a disk with ideal boundary and a marked point carrying a conical singularity with angle $\theta = 2\pi \beta$. For all $\beta>0$, we show that $\rm{Teich}^{\beta}(\overline{\mathbb D})\cong S^1\backslash \rm{Diff}(S^1)$, and we construct natural closed 2-forms $\omega_\beta$ induced by the Atiyah-Bott construction. For non-integer $\beta$, the form $\omega_\beta$ is symplectic, and one can identify $\rm{Teich}^{\beta}(\overline{\mathbb D})$ with the corresponding elliptic Virasoro coadjoint orbit. For positive integers $\beta=n$, $\omega_\beta$ is presymplectic, and it descends to the Kirillov-Kostant-Souriau symplectic form on… — Anton Alekseev, Rea Dalipi, Samson Shatashvili — arXiv math-ph / hep-th / arXiv math.GT / AT / SG / DG

item.title: Emergence of Topological Bound States in the Continuum via Stacking Trivial Bulks with Double Mirror Symmetry
item.description: Author(s): Chaohua Wu, Zhenxing Cui, Xuewei Zhang, Zuohong Wang, Mou Yan, and Gang Chen A surprisingly simple, symmetry-based trick perfectly traps waves without any energy leakage by cleverly stacking ordinary acoustic materials. [Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 226601] Published Wed Nov 25, 2026 — Chaohua Wu, Zhenxing Cui, Xuewei Zhang, Zuohong Wang, Mou Yan, Gang Chen — Physical Review Letters

item.title: Three-dimensional harmonic critical metrics for the Einstein-Hilbert functional and self-similar Ricci flows
item.description: We address the three-dimensional harmonic analogue of Hilbert's variational problem: does criticality of the Einstein-Hilbert functional under volume-preserving Chen-Nagano variations force constant sectional curvature, and how is this rigidity related to Ricci flow and topology? Starting from the known characterization of compact harmonic critical metrics as gradient Ricci solitons, we use Ivey's classification to show that such metrics on closed three manifolds are precisely the space-form metrics, equivalently the stationary metrics of the volume-normalized Ricci flow. We also describe residual gauge one-forms, establish transversality of the Chen-Nagano gauge to infinitesimal… — Sergey E. Stepanov, Irina I. Tsyganok — arXiv math.GT / AT / SG / DG

item.title: Rank-Two Attractors and Modularity for a Mirror Bicubic
item.description: We study the mirror family $\mathcal X_\lambda$ of the bicubic Calabi-Yau threefold, obtained from a family of complete intersections of two cubics in $\mathbb P^5$. We show that the four-dimensional weight-three Hodge structure of the fibers over $\lambda^6 = -8$ splits into two rational rank-two pieces of Hodge types $(1,0,0,1)$ and $(0,1,1,0)$; in particular, these points are rank-two attractor points. Using a Hesse pencil fiber-product realization, equivariant point counting, and the Serre-Faltings-Livne method, we identify their semisimplified $\ell$-adic Galois representations with those attached to the weight-four newform $f_{\mathsf{54.4.a.c}}$ and the Tate twist of the weight-two… — Yibing Chen, Emanuel Scheidegger — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Sharp boundary regularity for planar minimal graphs with analytic Dirichlet data
item.description: We study the boundary behavior of generalized (BV) solutions of the Dirichlet problem for the minimal surface equation over a bounded set \(\Omega\). Such a generalized solution is always the graph of a smooth function \(v\) inside \(\Omega\), but might carry a vertical part over \(\partial\Omega\), which records the gap between the prescribed Dirichlet datum \(g\) and the boundary trace \(h\) attained by \(v\). When \(\Omega\) is a bounded real-analytic planar domain and \(g\) is real analytic we prove that \(h\) is Lipschitz, right and left differentiable at every point, of class \(C^1\) on \(\partial\Omega\setminus\Sigma\), and real analytic on \(\{h\neq g\}\setminus\Sigma\), where… — Camillo De Lellis, Guido De Philippis, Alessio Figalli — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS / arXiv math.GT / AT / SG / DG

item.title: The Four-Loop Ladder Integral Family for the QED Electron Self-Energy
item.description: We compute the complete set of master integrals of the four-loop ladder integral family contributing to the electron self-energy in Quantum Electrodynamics. We obtain the results through canonical differential equations and write them as iterated integrals over integration kernels related to different parametrizations of the sunrise elliptic curve and a Calabi-Yau threefold. The rich structure of geometries and couplings between them requires the introduction of a large number of extra transcendental functions to reach $\epsilon$-factorization. We discuss explicitly how to find a canonical basis for a selection of particularly interesting sectors. Additionally, we compute local series… — Felix Forner, Andreas von Manteuffel, Christoph Nega, Lorenzo Tancredi — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Certified $p$-adic normal forms: an Eliasson-Vey theorem and zero sets of orbits
item.description: I use the Smith form of the homological operator to construct partial Poincar\'e-Dulac normal forms near an equilibrium of a vector field on $\mathbb {Z}_p^d$ with coefficients divisible by $p$ (by $4$ if $p=2$). Retaining the directions whose removal would cost more than a fixed number of digits gives convergence on an explicit ball for any linear part. For polynomial fields, an exact integer check of the conjugacy defect certifies the computed flow to $K$ digits in rescaled coordinates. When the quadratic parts of an integrable Hamiltonian system at a rank-$0$ point span a Cartan subalgebra, the homological divisors in symplectic eigencoordinates are integers. This lets me use Newton… — Kirill Terskii — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS / arXiv math.NT / AG / RT / arXiv math.GT / AT / SG / DG

item.title: The Lafforgue Transform
item.description: In this report, we survey the \emph{Lafforgue transform}, a natural representation-theoretic map from the Kazhdan cocenter to the Bernstein center of a reductive group over a local field. Its motivation comes from our study of the Braverman-Kazhdan proposal, a conjectural framework for establishing the meromorphic continuation and functional equations of general automorphic $L$-functions through harmonic analysis on possibly singular varieties. For $G=\SL_2$ and $\GL_2$, we explain how the stable part of the Lafforgue transform and its distinguished section are realized as integral transforms on the Steinberg-Hitchin base, with formulas of motivic nature that are valid over every local… — Zhilin Luo — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT

item.title: Nonlocal approximation of stable minimal surfaces with prescribed number of connected components
item.description: We show that every strictly stable classical minimal hypersurface in a Euclidean ball can be approximated, for $s$ sufficiently close to $1$, by a stable $s$-minimal surface in a smaller ball. We also give an explicit lower bound on the size of the interval of admissible values of $s$. As a consequence, we construct stable nonlocal minimal surfaces with an arbitrarily large number $k$ of connected components in a bounded region, under the quantitative condition $k \leq \frac{C}{\sqrt{1-s}}$, attaining an optimal result (at least in dimensions $2$ and $3$). As part of the proof of our main result, we obtain an auxiliary result of independent interest, providing quantitative estimates for… — Lorenzo De Gaspari, Serena Dipierro, Ovidiu Savin, Enrico Valdinoci — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS / arXiv math.GT / AT / SG / DG

item.title: Machine Learning for Calabi--Yau Geometry and Heterotic Compactification
item.description: Quantitative predictions from string compactification depend on geometric data that are difficult to compute analytically. This review surveys machine learning approaches to predicting topological properties of Calabi-Yau manifolds, discusses the search for new Calabi-Yau fourfolds, as well as numerical methods for approximating Ricci-flat metrics. In the context of heterotic compactifications, we explain how bundle metrics and harmonic matter forms enter calculations of canonically normalized Yukawa couplings and axion-matter interactions. We also outline applications to flux compactifications, warped and corrected backgrounds, and geometric structures beyond the Calabi-Yau setting… — Vishnu Jejjala, Damian Mayorga Pena — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Twisted K-Theory and Reduced Norms over Global and Higher Local Fields
item.description: We prove the Merkurjev--Suslin conjecture concerning reduced norms over both global and local fields. Furthermore, in both settings, we construct maps between truncated K-theory spectra that induce the reduced norms in degrees 1 and 2, and show that these maps are equivalences over local fields. Over global fields, we establish finiteness properties of their fibers and give a detailed description of their structure. We also extend the Merkurjev--Suslin conjecture to two-dimensional local fields and three-dimensional local fields with characteristic sequences (0, 0, 0) and (0, 0, p), and prove it in these settings. Finally, we apply these results to noncommutative class field theory over… — Hisato Matsukawa — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT

item.title: Asymptotics of Hitchin metrics and modularity of exceptional ALG gravitational instantons
item.description: We prove asymptotic estimates for the Hitchin metrics on four-dimensional moduli spaces of parabolic $\mathrm{SL}(n,\C)$-Higgs bundles on the three-punctured sphere with flag types corresponding to the Dynkin types $E_6$, $E_7$ and $E_8$. For fixed weights in the alcove interiors and fixed scalar graded residues, the Hitchin metric converges in $C^\infty$ to the semiflat metric along the end. The decay is polynomial in general and exponential when all graded residues vanish. For every admissible parameter with weights in the closed alcoves, the moduli space with its Hitchin metric is a complete nonflat ALG gravitational instanton of order two. Extending the period calculation of… — Shiyu Cao — arXiv math-ph / hep-th / arXiv math.GT / AT / SG / DG

item.title: On the chromatic splitting conjecture in coheight $1$
item.description: This article confirms predictions made by Hopkins' chromatic splitting conjecture in stable homotopy theory. A consequence of our main theorem is that a certain map of $K(h-1)$-local $\mathbb{E}_\infty$-rings $\mathbb{S}_{K(h-1)}^{B\mathbb{Z}}\to L_{K(h-1)}\mathbb{S}_{K(h)}$ admits a retract, so long as $p-1$ does not divide $h-1$. If $h=2$ and $p$ is odd, we show this map is an isomorphism. We use methods from the theory of $p$-divisible groups and $p$-adic geometry. Along the way we prove an entirely new kind of "two-tower isomorphism," in analogy with Faltings' isomorphism between the Lubin--Tate and Drinfeld towers, which parametrizes $p$-divisible groups over characteristic $p$… — Tobias Barthel, Lucas Mann, Rin Ray, Tomer M. Schlank, Andrew Senger, Jared Weinstein — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT / arXiv math.GT / AT / SG / DG

item.title: The inductive Galois-McKay conjecture for groups of Lie type C
item.description: We prove the inductive Galois-McKay conjecture for the symplectic groups. A key result is the determination of the character fields of the irreducible characters of the extensions of the symplectic group by field automorphisms. Two main ingredients for this are the theory of Brauer trees and the generalized Gelfand-Graev characters. — Lucas Ruhstorfer — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT

item.title: Flexible algebraic curves and fake vanishing cycles
item.description: We prove that complex curves in sufficiently ample linear systems on simply connected projective surfaces are topologically (spin) flexible: any (spin) mapping class of the underlying real surface extends to a topological mapping class of the ambient 4-manifold. As a corollary, we prove that smooth curves in the complex projective plane are topologically (spin) flexible. A consequence of topological flexibility is the existence of fake vanishing cycles, that is, simple closed curves on the underlying real surface that are not vanishing cycles, yet still bound a topologically embedded $(\pm1)$-framed disk in the surface exterior. We also give examples of pushed in Seifert surfaces in $D^4$… — Joshua Lehman, Tudur Lewis — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT / arXiv math.GT / AT / SG / DG

item.title: Rotationally symmetric fractional minimal surfaces
item.description: In this paper, we provide a non-trivial example of an $s$-minimal surface that is invariant under rotations. More precisely, we study alternating radial sets whose boundaries are finite or locally finite unions of concentric spheres and prove that, fixing the outer radius to $r=1$, there exists a radial configuration for which the fractional mean curvature $H_s$ vanishes at every free interface. We then show that rescaling radial maximizers by their innermost radius and passing to the limit yields a properly embedded, rotationally symmetric, locally finite hypersurface satisfying $H_s=0$ at every point of the boundary. — Chiara Gambicchia, Matteo Novaga, Matteo Talluri — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS / arXiv math.GT / AT / SG / DG

item.title: Symplectic bumpless pipe dreams
item.description: Bumpless pipe dreams are combinatorial objects in bijection with alternating sign matrices. Double Grothendieck polynomials can be expressed as weighted sums over bumpless pipe dreams, a perspective that has led to many advances in the combinatorics of Schubert calculus and connections with integrable systems. We introduce symplectic bumpless pipe dreams and present an analogous formula for symplectic Grothendieck polynomials, which represent the equivariant K-theoretic classes of Sp(2n)-orbit closures in the flag variety. To prove this result, we construct an analogue of Lascoux's inflation on these objects, providing a combinatorial realization of the symplectic transition equations that… — Zachary Hamaker, Anna Weigandt — arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.CC / cs.DM

item.title: Calabi-Yau fibrations and orbifold Mordell
item.description: We construct isotrivial projective families of Calabi-Yau varieties with arbitrarily large inf-multiplicities and no divisible fibres over the projective line. As an application, we show that any single instance of Campana's Orbifold Mordell Conjecture for a general-type C-pair of genus at most one (with only finite multiplicities) implies that the Weakly Special Conjecture is false. — Ariyan Javanpeykar — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT

item.title: Relativistic Hydrodynamics as an Intersection Problem
item.description: Ideal relativistic hydrodynamics admits a covariant description as an intersection problem in a symplectic space associated with spacetime. The independent fields are differential forms of degrees 0,1,3,4. Spacetime diffeomorphisms and shifts of the momentum one-form act Hamiltonianly; the zero locus of their moment map is a coisotropic subvariety encoding the transport equations. The spacetime metric and equation of state determine a Lagrangian submanifold, whose intersection with the coisotropic subvariety is precisely the Lichnerowicz--Carter system. We explain the geometric meaning of the canonical flow parameter, derive circulation and Ertel invariants directly from the constraints… — Nikita Nekrasov, Paul Wiegmann — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Exotic Universal Covers and Free Cyclic Actions from the Cartwright-Steger Surface
item.description: For every $m\geq2$, we construct a closed minimal symplectic four-manifold with fundamental group $\Z/m$, Euler characteristic $35$, and signature $1$. The construction is a genus-five symplectic sum of a blowup of the regular fourfold Cartwright-Steger cover and a cyclic Akhmedov-Park manifold. The gluing identifies the homomorphisms from the two surface groups to $\Z/m$. The universal cover is minimal symplectic and is homeomorphic but not diffeomorphic to $(18m-1)\CP\#(17m-1)\CPb$. It admits a free symplectic action of $\Z/m$. Intermediate quotients give examples with fundamental group $\Z/n$ and characteristic numbers $(e,\sigma)=(35k,k)$ for every $n\geq2$ and $k\geq1$. Using the same… — Anar Akhmedov, B. Doug Park, S\"{u}meyra Sakall{\i}, Sai-Kee Yeung — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT / arXiv math.GT / AT / SG / DG

item.title: Spin-Torsion Coupling: Vector and Scalar Torsional Potentials of Chiral Spinor Currents
item.description: We investigate integral representations of torsional fields sourced by chiral spinor currents within a weak-field, Ricci-flow-inspired geometric framework. Starting from the coupling between spinorial currents and axial torsion, we construct screened Green-kernel solutions and examine their relation to antisymmetric tetradic perturbations and contorsion. Particular attention is devoted to stationary toroidal configurations, for which the magnetic-type dipole moment vanishes while a nonzero toroidal moment and effective circulation remain. The dependence of these quantities on Yukawa screening is analyzed, together with their implications for an Aharonov-Bohm-like geometric structure. We… — Elisa Varani — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Periods, isomonodromy, and modularity of ALG/ALG$^*$ gravitational instantons
item.description: We prove that every smooth ALG or ALG$^*$ gravitational instanton of type $A_0,A_1,A_2,D_0,D_1,D_2,D_3$ is, up to homothety and hyperk\"ahler rotation, isometric to a rank-two wild Hitchin moduli space on $\PP^1$ with its $L^2$ metric. We compute the compact hyperk\"ahler periods and asymptotic parameters of these moduli spaces and give explicit inverse formulas for every admissible choice of these data. For the three ALG types, global isomonodromic transport realizes the two real parameters left undetermined by the compact periods. We use a Hamiltonian variation formula and uniform comparison with the semiflat metric to apply the Torelli and uniqueness theorems. — Shiyu Cao — arXiv math-ph / hep-th / arXiv math.GT / AT / SG / DG

item.title: Field-Dependent Kinetics, Exact Kinks, and a Moduli-Space Route from Self-Dual Yang-Mills Theory
item.description: We study scalar-field models in 1+1 dimensions with field-dependent kinetic coefficients, motivated by self-dual Yang-Mills (SDYM) theory as a generator of integrable equations. We derive the Euler-Lagrange equation, traveling-wave reduction, and first integral, and solve the inverse problem: given a kinetic structure and a prescribed tanh kink, which potential makes it exact? A quadratic spatial deformation with a canonical temporal sector yields a sextic potential. We obtain: (i) a closed-form kink energy with a Bogomolny-type formulation, independent of the odd parameter, which nonetheless shapes the energy density asymmetrically; (ii) vacuum curvature relations tying the spectrum to… — Ji Wang — arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Quasifibrations in \'etale homotopy theory
item.description: We study quasifibrations in \'etale homotopy theory and prove a criterion for a morphism of schemes to be a quasifibration in terms of its (higher) direct images for sheaves of sets and (possibly non-abelian) groups. This allows to generalise Friedlander's formula for the homotopy fibre of geometric fibrations to the case of an arbitrary qcqs base scheme that is not necessarily normal. Among the applications to geometric fibrations are (1) specialisation is an equivalence on the pro-$\Sigma$ completed profinite \'etale homotopy types of geometric fibres, (2) a long exact sequence of \'etale homotopy groups in characteristic 0, and (3) a partially $\Sigma$-completed exact sequence of… — Tim Holzschuh, Alexander Schmidt, Jakob Stix — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT

item.title: Fibered-knot braids and symplectic fake quadrics
item.description: We construct aspherical symplectic four-manifolds with the rational cohomology ring of $S^2\times S^2$ by summing ruled surfaces along braided multisections. For each $m\geq1$, we form two symplectic sums with the same gluing map in the chosen surface markings and normal framings, using a stabilized braid for the trefoil in one sum and for the torus knot $T(2,7)$ in the other. Both sums have integral first homology $({\mathbb Z}/2)^2\oplus{\mathbb Z}/(4m)$. Their fundamental groups admit respectively $36$ and $24$ epimorphisms onto $S_3$, so the sums are nonhomeomorphic. We also vary the gluing while keeping the multisections fixed. In each of five product, twisted, and hybrid cases, this… — Anar Akhmedov, B. Doug Park, Sai-Kee Yeung — arXiv math.GT / AT / SG / DG

item.title: Supercuspidal representations and types via double covers and the Fourier--Weil representation
item.description: We present a construction of supercuspidal representations and types for tame $p$-adic groups whose input is a generic essentially depth-zero representation of a double covers of twisted Levi subgroups. This clarifies and simplifies existing constructions by automatically producing and explaining the twisting quadratic character of Fintzen--Kaletha--Spice, the roots of unity in the Harish-Chandra character formula, and making the connection to the Galois side of the local Langlands correspondence immediate. The main innovation is the use of a Fourier model of the Weil representation defined on an extension of the symplectic group by the Witt group. — Jessica Fintzen, Tasho Kaletha — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT

item.title: Quaternionic geometry of symplectic and contact pairs
item.description: We introduce quaternionic analogues of symplectic pairs, contact--symplectic pairs and contact pairs. A hyper symplectic pair consists of three symplectic pairs whose sums form a positive quaternionic triple, while the contact analogues are defined through single or double symplectization. We prove that radial invariance of the induced complex structures is equivalent to the coincidence of the characteristic distributions, yielding a local product decomposition. Under a natural normalization, hyper contact--symplectic pairs are locally products of a $3$-Sasakian and a hyper-K\"ahler manifold and induce canonical $3$-quasi-Sasakian structures, whereas hyper contact pairs are locally… — Gianluca Bande, Beniamino Cappelletti-Montano — arXiv math.GT / AT / SG / DG

item.title: The generalized Franchetta conjecture for some hyper-K\"ahler varieties, III
item.description: The generalized Franchetta conjecture states that for a locally complete family of polarized hyper-K\"ahler varieties, the generically defined cycles on any fiber of the universal family over the moduli stack inject into cohomology via the cycle class map. We prove the generalized Franchetta conjecture for the family of double EPW sextics discovered by O'Grady and for the family of double EPW cubes discovered by Iliev-Kapustka-Kapustka-Ranestad. We also prove a Franchetta-type result for the relative square of the universal family of double EPW sextics, which allows to relate double EPW sextics and Gushel-Mukai fourfolds on the level of motives. The proof involves the geometry of… — Lie Fu, Robert Laterveer, Carl Mazzanti, Charles Vial — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT

item.title: Hodge cycles of Klein hypersurfaces
item.description: We study the space of Hodge cycles on Klein varieties. Relating it to the Hodge characters in a covering Fermat variety, we decompose the space of Hodge characters into a part generated by classes of rational subvarieties, and a non-trivial part which we call exceptional. Using Dirichlet characters we show that the exceptional part is always finite. Furthermore, we give sufficient conditions under which there are no exceptional characters, providing infinitely many new cases of the Hodge conjecture for Klein varieties. Finally, we describe the set of exceptional characters of Klein varieties for small dimensions. — Mario Pastrana, Roberto Villaflor — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT

item.title: Combinatorial relative orientability for toric and tropical geometry
item.description: Many problems in enumerative geometry are solved by computing the degree of the top Chern class of a suitable vector bundle. Results from $\mathbb{A}^1$-homotopy theory allow to answer enumerative questions over arbitrary fields, replacing the top Chern class by the Euler class in Chow-Witt groups. For its degree to be well-defined, one needs the vector bundle to be relatively oriented. Another way to solve enumerative problems is to translate them to tropical geometry, where they become combinatorial problems. In this paper, we give a combinatorial description of relative orientability for vector bundles over smooth proper toric varieties. We show that it behaves well under… — Nathan Tiggemann — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT

item.title: Brane Tilings and Polygons with Two Interior Points
item.description: We fully classify the brane tilings and the 4d N=1 supersymmetric quiver gauge theories corresponding to toric Calabi-Yau 3-folds whose toric diagrams are convex lattice polygons with two interior lattice points. There are 45 such polygons up to GL(2,Z) transformations and lattice translations: 5 triangles, 19 quadrilaterals, 16 pentagons and 5 hexagons. We identify all 323 toric phases corresponding to these toric Calabi-Yau 3-folds. For every toric phase, we present the brane tiling with its quiver and superpotential, the perfect matching matrix and the F- and D-term charge matrices. For each brane tiling, we study the mesonic moduli space of the corresponding abelian 4d N=1 theory… — Rak-Kyeong Seong — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: BMS Charges from Null Hypersurfaces
item.description: We show how the gravitational dynamics, phase space and Noether charges of the BMS group at future null infinity $\mathscr{I}^+$ can be derived as limits of their analogues on null hypersurfaces at finite distance. The Bondi mass-loss and angular-momentum evolution equations arise as limits of the Raychaudhuri and Damour constraints. The Ashtekar--Streubel (aka Wald--Zoupas) symplectic potential arises as a specific member of a two-parameter family of null-boundary symplectic potentials, corresponding to the Dirichlet (aka canonical) polarization, while the other members differ by field-space exact terms, leading to the same radiative pre-symplectic structure but potentially different BMS… — Martina Adamo, Luca Ciambelli, Felipe Diaz, Michael Imseis, Leonardo Sanhueza, Simone Speziale — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: A symplectic Hilbert hotel
item.description: We construct a smooth global symplectomorphism of an infinite dimensional separable Hilbert space mapping a ball of large radius to a subset of a cylinder of small radius. This symplectomorphism and its inverse map bounded sets to bounded sets. This example shows that Gromov's non-squeezing theorem does not generalize to infinite dimensional Hilbert spaces without further assumptions. — Alberto Abbondandolo — arXiv math.GT / AT / SG / DG

item.title: Equivariant Localization for $K(n)$-Local Gromov-Witten Invariants with Applications to Gopakumar-Vafa Invariants
item.description: For certain complex-oriented $K(n)$-local cohomology theories, we establish equivariant localization formulas for global Kuranishi charts and a Riemann-Roch formula. We apply these formulas to compute the genus-zero Gromov-Witten invariants of $\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^1}(-1)\oplus\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^1}(-1)$ at odd primes, obtaining a residue formula in terms of the formal group law of the chosen complex orientation. As an application, we derive a multiple-cover formula expressing the genus-zero Morava $K$-theoretic Gromov-Witten invariants of closed symplectic Calabi-Yau threefolds in terms of their Gopakumar-Vafa invariants. — Guangxi Yan — arXiv math.GT / AT / SG / DG

item.title: Gray II, K\"ahler Nullity and Ricci Flow on Generalized Flag Manifolds with Two Isotropy Summands
item.description: We investigate Gray's second curvature identity, K\"ahler nullity, and homogeneous Ricci flow on generalized flag manifolds with two isotropy summands. We prove that every invariant metric satisfies Gray's second identity for both invariant almost complex structures. For the non-integrable structure, the K\"ahler nullity is trivial except at a distinguished metric ratio, where it coincides with the vertical distribution of a homogeneous fibration. This distribution is integrable and has totally geodesic leaves. For the integrable structure, the K\"ahler nullity exhibits a different behavior and need not be integrable away from the K\"ahler locus. Finally, we reduce the normalized… — Lino Grama, Ailton R. Oliveira, Francisco V. Oliveira — arXiv math.GT / AT / SG / DG

item.title: Eigendecomposition for instantons via infinity-category
item.description: Suppose $L$ is a framed link in a balanced sutured manifold $(M, \gamma)$. We construct a link spectral sequence in sutured instanton homology. For properly embedded surfaces in $M$ disjoint from $L$, we refine the spectral sequence to preserve the induced multi-grading. We use $\infty$-categories to encode homotopical information from instanton theory. In particular, we obtain a simultaneous eigendecomposition of homotopy-coherently commutative operators on a chain complex or a hypercube complex. As the algebraic foundation for subsequent work of the second author and collaborators, we construct the mixed hypercube by combining the hypercubes of positive and negative bypass maps. This… — Longke Tang, Fan Ye — arXiv math.GT / AT / SG / DG

item.title: On the moduli space of nonpositively curved metrics on a product with a torus
item.description: We prove that if $N$ is a closed smooth manifold admitting a Riemannian metric of negative sectional curvature and $T^k$ is the $k$-dimensional torus, then there is a retraction from the moduli space of nonpositively curved Riemannian metrics on $T^k\times N$ onto the moduli space of flat metrics on $T^k$. As an application, we combine our retraction with Tuschmann and Wiemeler's work on the rational topology of the moduli space of flat metrics on $T^k$ to deduce that the moduli space of nonpositively curved metrics on $T^k\times N$ has nontrivial higher rational homotopy and cohomology groups when $k\geq5$. — F. Thomas Farrell, Yi Jiang — arXiv math.GT / AT / SG / DG

item.title: A decomposition of Hamiltonian matrices with symplectic kernels and its application to Williamson's diagonal form
item.description: In this paper, we establish a decomposition of Hamiltonian matrices with symplectic kernels, which extends the main result in [K. D. Ikramov, On the Symplectic Eigenvalues of Positive Definite Matrices. Moscow Univ. Comput. Math. Cybern., 42(2018)1-4]. As an application, we present another proof of Williamson's diagonal form for positive-semidefinite matrices with symplectic kernels. — Shaowu Huang, Yingxin Huang — arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Tame homotopy theory and the Goodwillie tower of the identity
item.description: The purpose of this note is to provide a modern treatment of Dwyer's tame homotopy theory and extend it to non-simply connected spaces, exploiting a connection with the work of Heuts on the Goodwillie tower of the identity. As an application, we construct spectral Lie algebraic models for Hess's $r$-mild homotopy theory. — Nicolas Gu\`es — arXiv math.GT / AT / SG / DG

item.title: A complete knot invariant from grid diagrams
item.description: Using grid diagrams, we define an infinite graph associated to each knot type. We prove that the isomorphism class of this grid graph is a complete invariant of the knot, up to mirroring. Even more, we prove that algorithmically determinable finite parts of this graph are enough to determine the knot type. — Agnese Barbensi, Daniele Celoria, Lavender Marshall, Finn Thompson — arXiv math.GT / AT / SG / DG

item.title: Comodule algebras and the cohomology of symplectic groups
item.description: We prove that the homology of symplectic groups with Steinberg module coefficients forms a comodule algebra over the homology of general linear groups with Steinberg module coefficients. We prove a freeness-type result for comodule algebras. We deduce new lower bounds for the high-dimensional cohomology of symplectic groups of number rings and their congruence subgroups. — Jeremy Miller, Urshita Pal, Peter Patzt — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT / arXiv math.GT / AT / SG / DG

item.title: Scaling limits for products of induced symplectic Ginibre matrices
item.description: We study the local eigenvalue correlations of products of independent induced symplectic Ginibre matrices in the large-dimensional limit. We establish the scaling limits of the correlation functions in the bulk, at the spectral edges, and outside the limiting spectral support, both near and away from the real axis. At regular spectral points, we show that the limiting correlations coincide with those of a single symplectic Ginibre ensemble, exhibiting Pfaffian structures near the real axis and determinantal structures away from it. At the origin, where the limiting spectral density develops a singularity, we derive an integral representation of the parameter-dependent limiting Pfaffian… — Can Atacan, Noah Ayg\"un, Yong-Woo Lee — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Non-local ergodic measures in symplectic dynamics
item.description: We consider the direct product of two symplectomorphisms, one of which exhibits a basic set and the other one acts on a compact surface and has a non-degenerate elliptic equilibrium. Under a local domination condition we show that a typical real-analytic perturbation of this system displays a large normally hyperbolic lamination on which the natural invariant measure is ergodic. The proof, which introduces a novel geometric source of semi-local ergodicity, combines tools ranging from KAM theory to geometric measure theory and is robust enough to be of interest in more general configurations. — Jaime Paradela — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS

item.title: Incidence Correspondences and Chow Motives in the Symplectic (Z/2Z)4-K3 Locus
item.description: We establish a Chow-motivic framework for projective K3 surfaces with a symplectic (Z/2Z)^4-action. For the universal Heisenberg-invariant quartic family, we show that the generically defined codimension-two cycles on the relative square are generated by three ambient classes and sixteen automorphism graphs, and that these nineteen classes are cohomologically independent. Combining this square-Franchetta property with a finite-cover trace construction and the Kuga-Satake correspondence, we prove that every smooth Heisenberg-invariant quartic K3 surface has a Chow motive of abelian type. We also consider the diagonal complete-intersection family of three quadrics and establish stability of… — Sixuan Gu — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT

item.title: Symplectic Matroids, Stabilizer Codes, and Quantum Secret-Sharing
item.description: An $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear $[[n,k]]_q$ stabilizer code is represented by a totally isotropic subspace of $\mathbb{F}_q^{2n}$ of dimension $n-k$, whose full-rank generator matrix has nonzero maximal minors on admissible column sets forming the bases of a representable symplectic matroid. Sarvepalli asked whether graphical symplectic matroids introduced by Chow give stabilizer codes with good parameters, when a Lagrangian matroid induces a quantum access structure, which code realizes it, and which polynomial carries the weight enumerator. We answer these questions. For a $3$-connected simple graph, every representation of a graphical symplectic matroid, over any field, gives a stabilizer code… — Sayantan Ganguly — arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.CC / cs.DM

item.title: The upward conformal limit
item.description: For a compact Riemann surface $X$, both the Higgs bundle moduli space and the de Rham moduli space have stratifications by holomorphic Lagrangian fibrations over the space of complex variations of Hodge structure. The $\hbar$-conformal limit gives a biholomorphic identification of the fibers of the two strata over a stable complex variation of Hodge structure. We introduce here the $\hbar$-upward conformal limit, which is the limit at infinity rather than at zero. The main results of this paper relate the irreducible components of the nilpotent cone on $X$, which are Lagrangian submanifolds, with Lagrangians in the Morse strata on $\bar{X}$, called zero velocity Lagrangians, via the… — Nerea Alonso-Garcia — arXiv math.GT / AT / SG / DG

item.title: Torsion order and the next-to-top term of knot Floer homology
item.description: Sivek conjectured that, for every nontrivial knot $K\subset S^3$, the dimension of the next-to-top term of $\widehat{\mathrm{HFK}}(K)$ is at least that of the top term. We show that this inequality holds for knots with $U$-torsion order one in either the minus theory $\mathrm{HFK}^-$ or the unoriented theory $\mathrm{HFK}'$. Combined with Eftekhary's work, this implies that knots with rational unknotting number one satisfy the conjecture. In particular, the result applies to every nontrivial satellite knot whose pattern can be unknotted in the solid torus by a single rational tangle replacement. — Kai Zhu — arXiv math.GT / AT / SG / DG

item.title: An $\infty$-category approach to $A_\infty$-algebras and $A_\infty$-categories
item.description: $A_\infty$-algebras over a commutative ring $R$ are generalizations of $R$-algebras in which multiplication is only associative up to higher homotopies. Similarly, $A_\infty$-categories over $R$ are generalizations of $R$-linear categories in which composition of morphisms is only associative up to higher homotopies. They are important in the definition of Fukaya categories in Symplectic Geometry, and in other areas of mathematics. By $\infty$-categories we mean quasicategories, a class of simplicial sets which are a model for $(\infty,1)$-categories, used in the work of Jacob Lurie. We define and study $\infty$-categories of $A_\infty$-algebras and $A_\infty$-categories. Our approach is… — Dominic Joyce — arXiv math.GT / AT / SG / DG

item.title: Quiver-Invariant Triality between Brane Brick Models
item.description: We study quiver-invariant triality between 2d (0,2) supersymmetric gauge theories described by brane brick models associated with toric Calabi-Yau 4-folds. The dual theories share the same gauge groups, field content and E-terms but have distinct J-terms. We present an explicit pair of such brane brick models and identify the sequence of triality mutations relating them. This sequence returns the quiver to its original form while transforming the J- and E-terms. We explain the relation between quiver-invariant triality and the orbifold reduction of quiver-invariant brane tilings. — Dongwook Ghim, Juno Kwon, Rak-Kyeong Seong — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: A Hopf algebra action on the cohomology of moduli of abelian varieties
item.description: We show that the rational compactly supported cohomology of the moduli space $\mathcal{A} = \bigsqcup_{g \geq 0} \mathcal{A}_g$ of principally polarized abelian varieties is free as a bigraded module over the Hopf algebra formed by its weight-zero subspace. The action arises from a symplectic analog of the Waldhausen $S$-construction. This structure yields new lower bounds for Betti numbers and the dimensions of the graded pieces of the weight filtration on the cohomology of $\mathcal{A}_g$. In particular, $\dim H_c^{2g + k}(\mathcal{A}_g)$ grows at least exponentially with $g$ for every nonnegative $k \neq 1, 3$. We also give conjectural descriptions of the full mixed Hodge structures in… — Urshita Pal, Sam Payne — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT / arXiv math.GT / AT / SG / DG

item.title: Actionless Branes on Axion Wormholes
item.description: Can a Euclidean axion wormhole extend to infinity with every instanton still suppressed? The imaginary distance bound says it cannot: some instanton must become actionless first. Calabi-Yau compactifications appear to violate the bound: several axions share the field excursion, and the instantons charged under any one of them stay suppressed all the way. We show that the wormhole can hide from these instantons but not from their bound states: misaligned central charges make a bound state cheaper than its constituents, while the axions act on every constituent. On the type IIB wormhole supported by two axions of the Neveu-Schwarz two-form, a fivebrane carrying string charge becomes… — A. Ramesh Chandra — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Grade Restriction Rule For D-Brane Transport In Non-Abelian Gauged Linear Sigma Models
item.description: We study the low energy behaviour of B-type D-branes in non-Abelian gauged linear sigma models. The main problem is to determine the grade restriction rule for D-brane transport from one phase to another along paths. We analyze the convergence condition of the integral for the hemisphere partition function. We perform a thorough analysis in a particular model with two phases, one weakly coupled and one strongly coupled, both corresponding to Calabi-Yau threefolds. General methods are developed in this study and are applied to other models successfully. The integrals for a set of special Chan-Paton representations exhibit critical behaviour around each singular point on the phase boundary… — Richard Eager, Kentaro Hori, Johanna Knapp, Mauricio Romo — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Calabi-Yau linear models with abelian bundles
item.description: We introduce a construction of (0,2) gauged linear sigma models whose large radius phases realize Calabi-Yau sigma models with line bundles. We study a family of such models admitting Landau-Ginzburg orbifold phases, described as asymmetric orbifolds of (2,2) Gepner models and free left-moving fermions. These orbifolds extend the Gepner construction to a broader class of (0,2) SCFTs, and reveal unexpected features, including the emergence of free fermions in twisted sectors and substantial enhancements of the left-moving current algebra. The gauged linear sigma model connects the Calabi-Yau geometry to these rational points, where the volume modulus becomes charged under the enhanced gauge… — Yann Proto — arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Self-adjoint skew quartics, symplectic monodromy, and zeta functions
item.description: For an odd prime power $P$, let $A_H(P)$ be the number of $a\in\F_{P^H}$ for which the self-adjoint skew quartic $t^4+t^3+at^2+t+1$ is irreducible in $\F_{P^H}[t;\sigma]$, with $\sigma(c)=c^P$. We determine $A_H(3)$ for every $H\ge1$ and prove that its minimal constant-coefficient recurrence has order $24$. Local ramification gives the degrees of the Steinberg and regular cuspidal Frobenius polynomials. Duality and finitely many exact counts determine both polynomials. For $P=p^f$ with $p\nmid f$, we construct an explicit genus-$P(P+1)/2$ flag curve whose zeta numerator is the Steinberg Frobenius polynomial. At $P=3$ this identifies the degree-$12$ factor computed above with the zeta… — Tomoya Hayata, Takahiro Tsushima — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT

item.title: Stein degree on birational log Calabi-Yau fibrations
item.description: We prove uniform bounds for the Stein degrees of boundary divisors on generalised log Calabi-Yau fibrations of Fano type over arbitrary fields of characteristic zero. The main ingredient is the birational case for which we provide two approaches. — Xintong Jiang, Santai Qu — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT

item.title: Functorial height and Orlov's rationality conjecture
item.description: An exceptional collection in the derived category of a smooth projective variety may fail to generate the whole category, and this failure cannot be detected by K-theory or by Hochschild homology. Kuznetsov's height detects it through Hochschild cohomology, that is, through natural transformations from the identity functor to its shifts. We replace the identity functor by an arbitrary endofunctor $F$ and define the height of a collection with coefficient $F$. It controls, in a range of degrees, the restriction of natural transformations $\mathrm{id}\to F$ to the orthogonal complement of the collection, and it is computed from the collection by a finite complex. For collections of line… — Xun Lin, Shizhuo Zhang — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT

item.title: On the refined Kaneko--Zagier conjecture
item.description: We extend our results on Zhao's conjectural basis to finite multiple zeta values modulo arbitrary prime powers and to the corresponding completed algebra. As a consequence, the refined Kaneko--Zagier conjecture, which gives a precise description of relations modulo arbitrary prime powers in terms of ordinary multiple zeta values, follows from the dimension and direct-sum conjectures for ordinary and finite multiple zeta values. We also prove Rosen's lifting conjecture under the dimension conjecture for finite multiple zeta values. The proofs use confluence relations and $p$-adic associators and do not use motivic theory. — Shin-ichiro Seki — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT

item.title: Convergence of the big J-function of a GKM manifold
item.description: The genus-$0$ equivariant Gromov--Witten (GW) invariants of a GKM manifold can be computed recursively by a recursion discovered by Brown and studied further by Coates--Corti--Iritani--Tseng. In this paper, we prove a slightly modified version of this result by realizing the J-function as a solution to a fixed-point problem. As an application, we prove that both the equivariant and the non-equivariant quantum cohomologies of a GKM manifold are convergent. We also show that the equivariant central charges have no poles in the spectral parameter, compute their monodromy and their asymptotics at $z=0$, and formulate an equivariant mirror symmetry conjecture for GKM manifolds. — Todor Milanov — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT
